items.summary: The June 16 economic brief is defined by the opening of the most consequential FOMC meeting of the 2026 cycle — Warsh's inaugural SEP/dot plot session — and the first confirmed market validation of the deal's deflationary impulse. The FOMC opened its June 16-17 meeting at standard schedule, in camera today; the rate decision, Summary of Economic Projections, and Warsh's inaugural press conference are all scheduled for June 17 2 PM ET. The rate decision is near-certain at 97-98% hold (3.50-3.75% range unchanged). The primary signal is the dot plot: FOMC publishing its first 2026 dot plot under Chairman Warsh, projecting member rate path expectations through 2028. The extraordinary complication: dot plot energy-CPI baseline assumptions were finalized before the June 14 deal declaration. May CPI stood at 4.2% YoY with gasoline up approximately 40% YoY — the dominant headline inflation driver. WTI opened approximately $81 Monday, down 4-5% from Friday's close (~$84-85) — the largest deal-attributed energy session of the 109-day arc. If MOU signs June 19 and oil sanctions are waived simultaneously, Iran's supply re-entry removes the single largest CPI driver in the fastest available timeline. The dot plot, finalized pre-Monday open, will be released with energy-CPI assumptions that may already be 30-40 annualized headline basis points stale. Three dot plot questions define market reaction June 17: (1) Does any member project a 2026 hike? Pre-deal late-2026 hike probability was tracking 65-70%; deal declaration materially compresses that — a dot showing any member's 2026 hike will be immediately contextualized as a pre-deal relic. (2) Does the committee show a first cut in 2026 (September window) or push entirely to 2027? (3) How does statement language characterize the energy-CPI channel? Warsh's June 17 press conference is the primary forward-signaling event: first time a Fed chair must address an active oil supply-shock resolution, its CPI implications, and the rate path simultaneously — with formal signing still 2 days away. April FOMC produced 4 dissents (most divided since 1992), creating statement-language complexity for Warsh's inaugural vote.

items.summary: Four secondary PNW environmental threads entering June 16 evening. First: NIFC above-normal Day 16 with heat event closing tonight; Juniper Dunes and Twin Sisters are the season's most concerning active fires under this outlook. East Cascades fire onset target (July, approximately T-13 from June 16) is being tested by the June 14-16 heat event — fuel drying under 95-100°F accelerates east Cascades ignition vulnerability; the July onset timeline may advance toward late June given the accelerated drying. Frontage Fire (Huntington, OR, I-84/Farewell Bend, 1,000 acres, partially contained) remains the leading named Oregon fire. Columbia Gorge is the secondary east-west corridor watch zone. BPA demand relief forecast: temperatures moderate Tuesday-Wednesday as heat warning expires tonight; brief grid resilience recovery window before next heat system. Second: NSF Newport OR at approximately 12 days to removal — the June 14-16 three-day heat event may be the last major atmospheric stress event the station fully instruments; July and August heat event forecasts will be degraded without Newport coastal data anchor; the station removal timeline is coinciding with peak summer high-consequence weather window, not preceding it. Third: Oregon gray whale washups at 21 YTD (Oregon coast), 17 YTD (Washington coast) — above expected annual pace; serious emaciation consistent with Pacific prey availability collapse; NOAA and NSF monitoring capacity declining concurrent with ecosystem stress requiring exactly that capacity. Fourth: drought baseline — Washington drought emergency Day 12 (4th consecutive year, 50% snowpack); Oregon drought monitor 83% coverage (12 county emergency); El Niño probability 61% (super El Niño 1-in-4); soil moisture deficits advancing under heat; BPA baseload tightening; seasonal fire risk envelope extends to October 2026.
